examples: I have breakfast at eight o'clock.
I don't have breakfast at seven o'clock.
I have breakfast with my family.

grammar_patterns.pattern: He gets up early. He doesn't get up late.
examples: He gets up early.
He doesn't get up late.
But jackaroos get up early every morning.

grammar_patterns.pattern: Does he [verb]? Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
examples: Does he live in a big house? Yes, he does.
Does Jim see a lot of snakes? Yes, he does.
Does Katie have a shower in the morning?
What time does he start work?
What time does Tom get up? He gets up at seven thirty.
What time does she have breakfast?

grammar_patterns.pattern: We catch the bus. They don't catch the train.
examples: We catch the bus.
They don't catch the train.
My mom and dad don't catch the bus to work.

grammar_patterns.pattern: Do you [verb]? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
examples: Do you walk to school? Yes, I do.
What time do you go to school?
Do your friends brush their teeth at night?

grammar_patterns.pattern: First, I [verb]. Then, I [verb]. Next, I [verb]. Finally, I [verb].
examples: First, I help on the farm.
Then, I watch my teachers on the Internet.
Next, I do my school work. Finally, I email my work to my teacher.

phonics.description: The oy sound as in boy and the oi sound as in coin.

key_sentences: Jim is our cousin in Australia. He's a jackaroo.
He gets up early every morning. He rides a horse and he looks after the sheep.
What time does Tom get up? He gets up at seven thirty.
Does he live in a big house? Yes, he does.
I get up early every day. First, I help on the farm.
Finally, I email my work to my teacher.
What time do you have breakfast? I have breakfast at seven forty-five.
